- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or shift mean down.
- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) and price is rising, model often over-optimistic; cap upward momentum or add downward buffer.
- After sharp spikes in sentiment or price, model frequently overshoots; apply lagged correction or reduce slope after peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, model may be too bullish; reduce forecast by 5–10% of peak value if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply downward bias in first 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model tends to ignore risk; force a conservative downward adjustment or add volatility buffer.
